text: Nothing, in their accredited capacity was done to-day by the two delegates from Canton, who, representing the four native Chambers of Commerce, are here in connection with arriving at a settlement of the boycott of Hongkong.

label: text
text: As Mr. Ho Kwong, chairman of the Twenty-four Commercial Guilds, informed the delegates yesterday, it is not exactly within the province of the Hongkong Chinese merchants to form organisations to decide how the "strike" is to be settled, the Hongkong Government having "initiated that this is a matter for the respective Governments. Still, the visit of the "peace mission" has had one beneficial effect. The air has been cleared, so to speak, for a continuation of the "conversation's" between the Hon. Mr. J. H. Kemp, as Hongkong's spokesman, and whoever is officially empowered to represent Canton. It will be recollected that these conversations—at which it was put plainly that Hongkong would not countenance strike pay—were adjourned sine die, to be resumed before any conference.

label: text
text:
Canton reports say that Mr. Eugene Chen, acting Foreign Minister, and Mr. Lu King-fo (who achieved a great deal as peace-maker in the Seamen's Strike) are to be Canton's official spokesmen.
Another point of view is this: It having been communicated to the Canton Government, by all classes in Canton, that a settlement is desirable, the officials will be able to take the initiative the more easily. A favourable report by Mr. Leung Pui-ki and Mr. Ma Pak-nin would be.

label: text
text: On the whole, it is felt that unless unforeseen circumstances arise, a conference will be held shortly between the two Governments, on a proper footing. What its outcome will be remains to be seen. The sponsors of this prediction is that the leading merchants in Canton now enjoy the Kuomintang's respect and goodwill to such an extent that Mr. Leung and Mr. Ma would not have been sent on a fruitless errand.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, in reply to questions, Mr. G. Locker-Lampson, Under-Secretary of State for the Colonies, said that by accepting the resolution on the Tariff Conference on November 19, His Majesty's Government was committed to agree to the insertion in the Treaty which the Conference was endeavouring to frame of an article granting China tariff autonomy on January 1, 1929. He said that up to the present, owing to the political disturbances in China, little progress had been made in drafting the Treaty. His Majesty's Government was not committed in any other respect.

label: text
text: Mr. Looker-Lampson added that the agreement of the Powers to grant tariff autonomy in 1929 and the "Chinese Government's undertaking" to abolish likin by then was not an article at present, but stood expressly interdependent. His Majesty's Government, before completing the negotiations, and not pleading for an actual grant of tariff autonomy, would undoubtedly expect China at least to initiate measures extending a fair hope of the ultimate abolition of likin.

text: The Freedom of the City of Edinburgh was conferred upon the Prime Minister to-day in the presence of a large gathering.

label: text
text: Presenting to Mr. Baldwin the silver casket containing the Freedom, the Lord Provost, Sir William L. Sleigh, said that the Prime Minister came fresh from one of the great triumphs of history. Mr. Baldwin was the man of the hour, and it was no small satisfaction to the citizens of Edinburgh that it had fallen to them to give him the first formal expression of the gratitude which all his fellow-countrymen owed him for the way in which he had successfully brought them through one of the greatest crises in their history.

text: An accident in which a toxic car crashed into a post near Status Square involving injuries to a passenger was recalled before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning when a Chinese motor car driver was charged with reckless driving. There was an additional charge against him of failing to notify his change of address.

label: text
text: Sub-Inspector Alexander termed this as a serious case of a motor car coming out of a side street into a main thoroughfare without giving a warning. He said that on May 25, shortly after midnight, the car came out of Wardley Street into Des Voeux Road and turned in an easterly direction. A taxicab which was then coming into town had to pull up suddenly to avoid a collision, but skidded and ran into a post. Sub-Inspector McLennan who was a passenger in the taxi, was injured and had been nine days in hospital.

label: text
text: Although not quite recovered from his injuries, Sub-Inspector McLennan was present in Court and intimated that he did not wish to bring any claim for compensation.

label: text
text: Defendant was fined $10 on the charge of failing to notify his change of address. The other charge, the Magistrate said, was a very serious one which might have involved loss of life and actually caused injuries to a police officer. He would be fined $100.

label: text
text: A charge of causing obstruction with his motor car at Pedder Street on May 29 was preferred against Professor Faid, of the Hongkong University. He pleaded ignorance of the regulations and was fined $5.

label: text
text: The offence of allowing a learner to have control of a car in a public thoroughfare resulted in a summons against the licensed driver. The learner was also charged with driving without a licence.

label: text
text: Sub-Inspector Alexander pointed out the danger by stating that the car was being driven past the Naval Dockyard just at a time when crowds of employees were leaving for their noon-day meal.

label: text
text: Fines of $15 on the driver and $10 on the learner were imposed.

label: text
text: News has been received in Hongkong of the recovery from the river of the body of Mr. J. M. Phillips, manager of the A.P.C. branch at Nanning, whose capture by bandits near Taiping was reported a week or so ago. Mr. Phillips at the time was on his way to Nanning from Lungchow. A body of troops was reported at the time to have been despatched from Lungchow to locate the bandits and effect the release of Mr. Phillips, and it is presumed that the bandits in the course of their retreat killed their captive and disposed of the body.

label: text
text: Mr. Philips, who was about 24 years of age, came out with the Company about two years ago and was stationed for a time at Wuchow. The district in which he was captured has gained notoriety in connection with the activities of bandits which infest that area.
